This section takes effect in daily work immediately upon issue and must be followed without delay.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the minimum standard for handling companion animal travel matters so that every case is processed safely, promptly, and with calm instruction.

All staff must treat each traveler with courtesy and urgency, confirm carrier condition before acceptance, and coordinate with the ground team whenever an animal must be moved between services. Keep guidance brief, kind, and actionable, and never leave a customer uncertain about the next step. If Samuel Costa or Ethan Ali presents a booking with a pet, record the traveler details clearly, verify the carrier meets current acceptance rules, and make sure the handoff is understood by all involved staff. The pet must remain secure, the paperwork must be complete, and no employee may promise an exception without approval from the senior coordinator.

When a traveler asks about lounge access, give only approved information and avoid speculation. <<FACT F002>> The lounge area must be checked for cleanliness, safe entry, and quiet conditions before any animal is directed there, and staff must intervene at once if a carrier is damaged, wet, or improperly closed. <<FACT F019>> If a traveler has a concern about feeding, hydration, medication, or stress, respond at once with the approved procedure and escalate any medical concern without delay.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk must log every exception, refusal, reroute, and incident in the service record before the end of the duty period. Do not rely on memory, informal notes, or verbal handoffs alone. Protect customer privacy, speak only with authorized personnel, and keep all communication accurate, direct, and respectful. If a pet such as Loki shows signs of distress, reduce noise around the carrier, maintain steady supervision, and notify the appropriate lead immediately so that the matter is handled correctly.

Any uncertainty, conflict, or safety concern must be escalated at once to the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor.
